english: Come, sit close to me. Listen to me. I'll tell you. My grandfather's name was Eliezer Simhaev. He was born in the city of Bukhara in 1840 to the family of Simha and Rivka. In the past people didn't have last names. His last name became Simhaev because his father was Simha.

english: You had told me that your grandfather was from the city of Kokand.

english: Yes, but then in his youth my grandfather moved to Kokand.
bukhori: Hov, ba'd ba soloyi yoshigeshon bovom ba Qüqon küchidin.

english: What did he use to do there?
He worked in commerce. He was a merchant of the First Guild, a very rich man. He himself was a kind person; he had green eyes and red hair.
bukhori: Shon kori savdogari mekadin. Savdogari yakumi gildiya, odami boy-badavlat budin. Xudashon odami nek budin, chashmoyi kavüd va müyi mala doshtin.

english: That is why the Muslims gave him the name Malaboy. The meaning of this nickname is a wealthy man with red hair. He became well known by this name.
bukhori: A broyi hamin, musulmono ba ü nomi Malaboy dodan. Ma'noyi hamin laqam - boye ki müyi mala dora. Hamin nom qati bovom bisyor nomdor shudin.

english: Did you see your grandfather yourself?

No, I didn't see my grandfather, because he fled to Jerusalem in 1921 after the revolution. But I know that my grandfather, may his soul rest in peace and his place be in Gan Eden, was a noble person and a benefactor. People respected him greatly. For fifty years he was the head of the Jewish community of the city of Kokand. Later a university was opened in his house.
bukhori: Ne. Ma bovoma nadidam, abaski ü ba'di inqilov ba soli 1921 ba Yerusholayim gurext. Lekin man medonam, ki bovom, Xudo rahmat karda bosha, joshon ba Gan-'Eden bosha, odamshavanda, misvodüst budin. Miyoni odamo bisyor ovrüyu 'izat doshtin. Panjo sol ü kalontari jamo'ati isroeli shari Qüqon budin. Ba'd xoneshonba universitet vo shud.

english: How many children did Malaboy have?

My grandfather Malaboy with my grandmother Rachel Uvadeva had seven children: Aboi Mala, Bulur, Imashalom, Miriam, my father Yehuda-Ari (Meli), Israel, and Bakhmal. My uncle Abo was a kind, rich, noble person, an aristocrat, a merchant of the First Guild, and had several factories. He was helping the Jews, but was a gambler. His wife Betty was a daughter of Hayim Wadiaef. Both of my aunts married Wadiaef sons: Miriam married Sion son of Haim Wadiaef and Bakhmal married Rafael son of Izhak-Baruch Wadiaef.
bukhori: Bovom, Malaboy, bivim Rohel Uvadeva qati hafta bacha doshtin: Aboyi Mala, Bulür, Imosholüm, Miryom, Yahudo-Ari (Meli) - dadim, Isroel, Baxmal. Abo 'amakam odami nek, boy-badavlat, odamshavanda, asilzoda, savdogari gildiyi yakum budin, chandta fabriku zavod doshtin. Ba juuto yordam medodin, lekin qartaboz bu. Zanash, Bitiyo, duxtari Hayim Vadyaev bu. Duta 'amom ba duta farzandoyi Vadyaefo rasidan. Miryom ba Sion ben Hayim Vadyaev va Baxmal ba Rafoel ben Isok-Borux Vadyaev.

english: Did all of them live in Kokand?

Yes. My dear, you are still young, but know that most of the rich merchant families lived in Kokand. The richest among the Bukharian Jews were the Wadiaef brothers, then Rafael Poteliakhov, and then the Simhaevs. These three rich families became double in-laws with each other.
bukhori: Hov. Joni bivesh, tu hole yosh, lekin don ki bisyortarini mishpohoyi boyi savdogaro Qüqonba meshishtan. Akayu uka Vadyaefo a hama juuto boyi kalon budan, ba'd Rafoel Potelyahov va ba'd Simhaefo. Ino, seta mishpohoyi 'osheri godül miyoneshon qarchi qudo shudan.

english: From which family was your mother?

My late mother was from Tashkent. She was a daughter of a rich man of Tashkent - Isachar Davidov - and Bonu Abramov (from the family of the 40 Girls). In that time rich people used to marry among themselves. That is how my mother went from Tashkent to Kokand. Their matchmaker was Rayhon Bulbul (Nightingale) Yagudaev.
bukhori: Onim, rahmati, a Toshkan budin. Ü duxtari boyi Toshkan - Isoxor Davidov va Bonu Abramov (a avloti Qirq Qiz). Unvaxt odamoyi boy miyoni xudashon qudo meshudan. Haminxel onim a Toshkan ba Qüqon raftin. Xosgori ino Rayhoni Bulbul Yagudaev bu.

english: Thanks, dear grandmother. Your story was very interesting. Now I know who we are and where we're from.
bukhori: Rahmat bivijon. Gavaton bisyor qiziq. Aknun ma famidam: ki mo hastim va a gjo omadim.

notes: The Navera-Bivi dialogue is based on a real conversation of the author with his grandmother Yekaterina Simhaeva (1916-2005).

Present-future conjectural (me- + past participle + -gi + ending) gives might in the present or future: Man meraftagi, I might go.
Present-progressive conjectural (rafsoda + -gi + ending) gives might be doing: Man rafsodagi, I might be going.
The future participle (infinitive + -i + hast + ending) gives the meaning want: Man guftani hastam, I want to say. In conversation hast + ending may not be pronounced.
